template:
You write ONE detection rule for a security measurement lab. Reply with exactly one JSON object, the rule, and nothing else: no prose, no code fence.

The brief (it describes an attack technique and a legitimate twin activity; both run as an unprivileged job user in a Linux VM without network):
{BRIEF}

What the rule sees. The VM records every exec of the job with auditd, turned into JSON events by Laurel. A rule is judged on ONE event at a time and fires if it is true on any event of a run. It must fire on runs of the technique and on no event of the twin's runs. Below is one real event from a different, unrelated job, to show the shape (some file attributes cut):
{EXAMPLE}
Notes on the shape: EXECVE.ARGV is the list of argument strings as typed (argv[0] is the program name as typed, e.g. "cat", not "/usr/bin/cat"). SYSCALL.ARGV holds raw register values, not arguments. PATH is a list of the files the exec touched. A field path that reaches a list tests each element.

The rule language:
- A rule is {"any": [leaf, ...]} (true if at least one leaf is true) or {"all": [leaf, ...]} (true if every leaf is true). No nesting.
- A leaf is {"field": [key, key, ...], "op": "eq" | "contains" | "has", "value": ...}: field is the path of keys into the event, e.g. ["EXECVE", "ARGV"] or ["SYSCALL", "comm"].
- "eq": the value at the path (or some element of a list there) equals value; value is a string or an integer.
- "contains": the string at the path (or some string element of a list there) contains value as a substring; value is a string.
- "has": the path exists; this op takes no value.

Example of the format only (it detects nothing useful): {"all": [{"field": ["EXECVE", "ARGV"], "op": "eq", "value": "true"}, {"field": ["SYSCALL", "UID"], "op": "has"}]}
how: The prompt for a pair is the template with {BRIEF} replaced by the pair's brief and {EXAMPLE} by example_event as written by json.dumps(indent=1) plus a newline. Every author gets that prompt once per sample, in an empty directory, tools off where its CLI allows, no retry; an answer that is not one rule is a recorded failure.
